To align the caption of a table to the left in LaTeX without using the `caption` package, you can manually adjust the caption by using the `\raggedright` command within the `\caption` command context.

Here’s an example of how to do this:

```latex
\documentclass{article}

\begin{document}

\begin{table}[ht]
    \centering
    \begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|}
        \hline
        Header 1 & Header 2 & Header 3 \\
        \hline
        Value 1 & Value 2 & Value 3 \\
        \hline
    \end{tabular}
    \caption{%
        \raggedright
        This is a left-aligned caption. It is aligned to the left without using the caption package.
    }
    \label{tab:leftalignedcaption}
\end{table}

\end{document}
```

### Explanation:

- The `\raggedright` command ensures that the text following it (in this case, the caption text) is left-aligned.
- Placing `\raggedright` inside the `\caption{...}` directly allows you to achieve the left alignment effect without needing to load any additional packages.

### Note:

- This approach has limitations, and you might not have fine control over caption formatting compared to using the `caption` package, which is recommended for more complex tables or advanced formatting options.
